item.title: 2. Bundesliga: Heidenheim end winless run with convincing victory over Nürnberg
item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Heidenheim end winless run with convincing victory over Nürnberg Frank Schmidt’s side made the perfect start when Patrick Mainka headed home from a corner in the 13th minute. However, Nürnberg restored parity shortly before half-time through a Marcel Costly own goal, setting up an intriguing second half. The visitors started the second period brightly, with Julian Justvan striking the post in the 49th minute after being teed up by William Bøving. Justvan also went close from distance later in the half, rattling the crossbar as Nürnberg searched for a breakthrough. Despite that promising spell, Heidenheim regained control of the contest and restored their advantage in the 61st minute. Following a Nürnberg throw-in that the visitors failed to clear, Tim Siersleben laid the ball back to Budu Zivzivadze, whose effort took a significant deflection off Fynn Otto before finding the net. The goal was subsequently allowed to stand following a VAR review for a possible offside. Heidenheim quickly added a third to put themselves firmly in the driving seat. In the 65th minute, Jan Schöppner initially saw his header from a Paul Hennrich cross saved by Jan Reichert, but the midfielder reacted quickest to convert the rebound from close range. Nürnberg attempted to find a route back into the game, with Justvan particularly unfortunate to see another effort strike the woodwork. The visitors were also denied when a mishit cross from Porstner struck the upright in the 81st minute. Heidenheim remained defensively organised during the closing stages, with Sirlord Conteh also seeing an effort blocked by Alexios Kalogeropoulos after being played into the penalty area by Alessandro Vogt. Four minutes of additional time offered Nürnberg little opportunity to mount a comeback, as Heidenheim comfortably saw out the remainder of the contest. The victory represents an important result for Schmidt’s side, who had gone seven consecutive league matches without winning. All three of their goals came from set-pieces, highlighting the effectiveness of their delivery and aerial threat. For Nürnberg and head coach Miroslav Klose, meanwhile, it is a second consecutive defeat after last weekend’s 2-1 home loss against Eintracht Braunschweig. Despite creating several opportunities, the visitors were ultimately made to pay for their defensive shortcomings and inability to take advantage of their second-half pressure.

item.title: José Mourinho on ‘generational’ Jude Bellingham and Zinedine Zidane comparisons
item.description: José Mourinho labeled Jude Bellingham 'one of the best players of his generation' -Credit:Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images Jude Bellingham may only be 23 years old, but he has already drawn comparisons with one of Real Madrid’s all-time greats, fellow No. 5 and FIFA World Cup winner, Zinedine Zidane. Such remarks were only amplified following the Englishman’s remarkable - perhaps even Puskás Award-worthy - goal in Los Blancos’ 5-1 comeback win in the UEFA Champions League against Eredivisie champions PSV on Tuesday. A halftime substitute alongside Ibrahima Konaté and Dean Huijsen, Bellingham followed up Federico Valverde’s 50th-minute equalizer with a stunning outside-of-the-boot strike to give Madrid the lead. The former Borussia Dortmund star’s shot quickly went viral, with his younger brother and fellow Three Lions international Jobe jokingly suggesting on CBS Sports that the shot ‘came off his shin.’ Andoni Iraola provides Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo, and Ryan Gravenberch derby updates Wrexham's unofficial 'One of Our Own' is paying back Phil Parkinson's faith perfectly Bellingham has scored seven goals so far this season -Credit:Burak Akbulut/Anadolu via Getty Images Kylian Mbappé subsequently scored a brace while Vinícius Júnior scored a fifth, via a Bellingham assist, as Madrid maintained their perfect League Phase record after five games. Following Bellingham’s latest heroics and ahead of Saturday’s La Liga visit from ninth-placed Deportivo Alavés, Madrid boss José Mourinho was quizzed on the England star. While the Portuguese coach wasn’t shy to laud the abilities of the midfielder, he stopped short of comparing him to France icon Zidane. “I don't like to compare players from different generations,” he said, via ESPN . “Zidane was one of the best in the world of his generation. Jude is already one of the best players of his generation. I don't like to compare.” Bellingham is yet to miss a game since Mourinho’s return to the Santiago Bernabéu dugout this summer, playing the second-most league minutes behind only leading goal scorer Mbappé (13) - who is just two goals behind Barcelona’s Raphinha in the race for the Golden Boot. “The reason Kylian and Jude have played so many minutes isn't their names, or a rule,” Mourinho commented. “It's their performance. If their performance is incomparable with what another player can do, that makes the difference. We feel what it's like to play with, and to play without, Jude.” To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE In 18 appearances across all competitions, Bellingham has found the back of the net seven times, providing a further five times, all whilst failing to be named to the starting XI just twice. Madrid currently sit second in La Liga on 33 points after 13 games, just two behind Hansi Flick’s reigning back-to-back champions Barça, and two ahead of crosstown rivals Atlético Madrid. item.description: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After a trio of games on Thanksgiving, we’re getting a Friday afternoon matchup in Week 12, featuring the Denver Broncos (8-2) on the road against the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4). The Broncos lead the all-time series between these teams, 15-11-1, but the Steelers have won their three most-recent meetings. They last faced off back in 2024, when the Steelers won on the road in Denver, 13-6. This will be an interesting evening for Steelers fans, who have had a whirlwind week with Aaron Rodgers being benched and then the QB going on the Pat McAfee show to expose head coach Mike McCarthy’s incompetence. The locker room is dealing with a dumpster fire — as revealed by Mike Tomlin on Sunday night — and that drama could end up affecting how they play on Friday. item.title: Alabama’s SEC Championship Game Scenarios Explained
item.description: TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - NOVEMBER 21: Wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams #1 of the Alabama Crimson Tide celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the first half of their game against the Chattanooga Mocs at Bryant-Denny Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Michael Chang/Getty Images) Getty TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - NOVEMBER 21: Wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams #1 of the Alabama Crimson Tide celebrates with quarterback Austin Mack #10 of the Alabama Crimson Tide after scoring a touchdown during the first half of their game against the Chattanooga Mocs at Bryant-Denny Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Michael Chang/Getty Images) ATHENS, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 22: Chris Cole #9 reacts with Joseph Jonah-Ajonye #99 of the Georgia Bulldogs during the third quarter against the Charlotte 49ers at Sanford Stadium on November 22, 2025 in Athens, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) Alabama is still alive in the hunt for a spot in the final SEC Championship Game. The Crimson Tide will need multiple things to go their way on the final weekend of the regular season to make that happen, including a positive result in the Iron Bowl against Auburn. Texas and Tennessee are also involved in the final equation. Alabama’s SEC Championship Game Scenarios Getty TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA – NOVEMBER 21: Wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams #1 of the Alabama Crimson Tide celebrates with quarterback Austin Mack #10 of the Alabama Crimson Tide after scoring a touchdown during the first half of their game against the Chattanooga Mocs at Bryant-Denny Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Michael Chang/Getty Images) There are essentially two scenarios for Alabama, one much more likely than the other, but neither particularly probable. Alabama needs three things to happen this weekend in the more likely possibility: Alabama beats Auburn. Texas A&M beats Texas. Vanderbilt beats Tennessee. That’s because both Texas and Tennessee hold tiebreakers for having beaten Alabama, so since they enter the weekend with tied records in SEC play, Alabama needs to one-up them this weekend. However, there’s another scenario: a three-way tie. In a three-way tie, head-to-head can’t be used as the main tiebreaker, and CBS Sports revealed that the SEC would come down to its fourth tiebreaker, the cumulative SEC winning percentage of each of the three-way tied team’s conference opponents. If all three of Alabama, Texas and Tennessee win this weekend, Alabama can make the SEC title game if: Mississippi State beats Ole Miss. LSU beats Arkansas. The latter is much more likely there than the former. So there’s a chance. If Alabama loses on Saturday, the tiebreakers won’t work in its favor no matter what else happens. Who Would Alabama Play in SEC Title Game? item.title: Steelers fans hand out ice cream sandwiches at tailgate amid Rodgers-McCarthy saga
item.description: Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers fans can finally turn their focus back to matters on the field this Black Friday, with the Denver Broncos in town for their Week 12 clash. It has been quite the week in Pittsburgh, which has seen Aaron Rodgers released from the organisation and leave a trail of destruction behind him. Head coach Mike McCarthy has come under huge scrutiny from Rodgers, which has been the biggest talking point of the season so far. Rodgers accused McCarthy of a number of different things, with another former Steelers player suggesting that the veteran head coach has someone inside the building who provides him with ice cream sandwiches on demand. Pittsburgh Steelers fans hand out ice cream sandwiches at pre-Broncos tailgate Friday’s game against the Broncos is going to be hugely important for the Steelers , following their back-to-back defeats leading to the remarkable scenes earlier this week. Steelers fans are choosing to make light of the situation inside the building, though. A video was shared on X ahead of the game at Acrisure Stadium showing fans at the pre-game tailgate handing out ice cream sandwiches. There are weather concerns in Pittsburgh, but this week’s events have provided too big an opportunity for these fans to pass up. “We’ve got Mike McCarthy’s assistant right here, baby,” one of the fans said to the camera. Considering the mess that has been left behind by Rodgers inside the Steelers’ building, it is great to see these fans making light of the events. Friday’s game against the Broncos has an awful lot riding on it, but these fans are clearly determined to have a good time. item.title: Klinsmann defends comments by Hoeness, Rummenigge about Musiala
item.description: FILE PHOTO — Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala in action during the UEFA Champions League group stage soccer match between Lille and Bayern Munich at Stade Pierre-Mauroy. (is associated with: «Klinsmann defends comments by Hoeness, Rummenigge about Musiala») Sven Hoppe/dpa Former Germany national trainer Jürgen Klinsmann came out in defence of comments made by Bayern Munich bosses Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge over the health of international attacker Jamal Musiala on Friday. "I think this is also kind of a bit of German culture. We're known for going straight in the face of people and we just say something we feel in that moment," the former Bayern coach told US sports channel ESPN. "We don't actually mean it in a mean" way, he added. Musiala made his comeback last week from a torn muscle fibre that sidelined him for one and a half months, but suffered yet another setback. He was sidelined on Friday until further notice due to a muscle injury in his right thigh. The player has struggled with fitness since he broke his fibula during the Club World Cup in 2025. Besides that, Musiala revealed earlier this year that he suffers from absence seizures. His health condition sparked debate after Bayern supervisory board members Hoeness and Rummenigge raised the prospect of the midfielder taking a pay cut because of his health problems. The suggestion was widely slammed, including by Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich and former Bayern board member Oliver Kahn. The two also publicly questioned whether Musiala, one of Bayern's top earners with a contract running until 2030, could return to his previous level of performance. But of the controversial comments made, Klinsmann said the aim was actually "to bring up the topic and have an open eye-to-eye discussion and make both parties understand." Abroad, this might be perceived differently, he said. "But this is the way sometimes we communicate ... It's also a little bit in our DNA," Klinsmann said. 'They don't mean any harm to Musiala' "Sometimes, I think these comments are given a dynamic then," he said. "I don't think that Uli Hoeness or Karl-Heinz Rummenigge want to damage him in any way," said Klinsmann. "Maybe inside they are a bit frustrated, have concerns. But they don't mean any harm to Jamal Musiala." Klinsmann recalled his playing days at FC Bayern, "when we'd sometimes have fights in the locker room, verbally, face to face, where we just needed to get it out. Sometimes not really nice words but we got it out and we felt better about it afterwards." For Musiala, this is currently "a very, very difficult period of his career. It's an illness that's very difficult to deal with. We all hope for him that he'll get better and better step by step and is 100% again," said Klinsmann

item.title: France slips into ‘technical recession’ after GDP revision
item.description: France’s economy has slipped into a technical recession after revised official figures showed that gross domestic product (GDP) contracted in the third quarter, extending the country’s economic decline. The National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) said on Friday that the eurozone’s second-largest economy shrank by 0.2 per cent in the third quarter, revising its initial estimate of a 0.1 per cent contraction. The agency also revised second-quarter growth downwards to 0.02 per cent from zero per cent previously, although the figure was rounded to zero in the headline data. The revisions mean France’s economy has recorded consecutive quarterly contractions since the end of last year, meeting the conventional definition of a technical recession, which is two successive quarters of negative economic growth. The latest figures pose additional challenges for the government as it struggles to rein in the country’s budget deficit, with its target of 0.5 per cent economic growth this year now appearing increasingly difficult to achieve. The minority government is also facing difficulties securing parliamentary approval for its 2027 budget, which seeks to reduce the fiscal deficit from 5.4 per cent of GDP this year to five per cent next year. The budget debate comes five months before France’s presidential election, amid deep divisions in parliament. Reacting to the figures, Finance Minister Roland Lescure called for the speedy adoption of the budget, insisting that the five per cent deficit target was non-negotiable. “We must adopt a budget as soon as possible with a non-negotiable deficit target of 5%. It is imperative that we restore visibility for economic stakeholders,” he said. A breakdown of the third-quarter GDP figures by INSEE showed that weak domestic demand contributed to the contraction. Consumer spending rose by 0.3 per cent, but this was offset by a 0.8 per cent decline in business investment. The rebuilding of business inventories contributed 0.3 percentage points to GDP growth, following a 0.7 percentage-point reduction in the previous quarter. Foreign trade also weighed heavily on economic performance, subtracting 0.6 percentage points from output as exports fell by 1.6 per cent while imports increased by 0.1 per cent. Despite the contraction, the Bank of France said earlier in November that the economy was expected to record moderate growth in the fourth quarter. item.title: Kebbi Police probe alleged importation of political thugs
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has launched an investigation into a viral video showing suspected political thugs brandishing dangerous weapons and issuing threats capable of undermining public peace and security in the state. The command also said it had invited three persons mentioned in the video for questioning over the circumstances surrounding the presence of the suspected thugs in Kebbi State. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, saying intelligence reports and preliminary scrutiny of the video identified one “Mai Barewa”, described as a notorious thug from Sokoto State, alongside other individuals wielding dangerous weapons and making threatening statements. According to Usman, the individuals were heard in the video claiming to have responded to an invitation and mentioning three persons identified as Manu Gwanna, Bashar S. A. and Khairullah Jega in connection with their presence in the state. He described the threats, particularly those directed at individuals perceived not to support the ruling party, as a potential recipe for political violence. The police spokesman said the persons mentioned and identified in the video had been invited to assist the ongoing investigation, while the command was taking steps to identify, apprehend and prosecute Mai Barewa and his accomplices. He said the police would ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. The command reiterated its commitment to political neutrality, impartial law enforcement and the protection of all citizens, irrespective of their political affiliations. It warned that no political party, individual or group would be allowed to undermine peaceful electioneering, intimidate citizens or engage in violence under the guise of political activities. The statement noted that Kebbi had long enjoyed a peaceful political climate, which must be preserved ahead of the 2027 general elections. Consequently, the police warned political parties, their leaders, supporters and associates against recruiting, harbouring, mobilising or sponsoring suspected imported thugs, or engaging in any conduct capable of inciting violence and disrupting political stability. The command further warned that it would not allow political violence, intimidation and lawlessness to take root in the state or set a dangerous precedent ahead of the 2027 elections. It urged residents to remain calm, refrain from taking the law into their own hands and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest police station or through the command’s designated communication channels. The police assured residents of its commitment to maintaining peace, protecting lives and property, and ensuring that all political activities in the state are conducted within the ambit of the law. item.title: 2027: Nasarawa translates INEC messages into local languages
item.description: Government targets rural communities ahead of Saturday’s mock exercise By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has commenced the translation and dissemination of Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) public enlightenment messages into Hausa and other major indigenous languages to sensitise residents ahead of Saturday’s nationwide mock accreditation and results upload exercise. The Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr. Nawani Aboki, disclosed this on Friday while briefing journalists in Lafia ahead of the exercise, saying the grassroots sensitisation campaign was designed to remove language barriers and ensure that rural communities understood the electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to Aboki, the ministry has produced and commenced airing public service announcements listing the 294 polling units selected for the exercise in Nasarawa State. He said radio jingles had also been produced in English, Hausa and local dialects as part of efforts to complement INEC’s voter education campaign, in line with Governor Abdullahi Sule’s commitment to supporting the Commission’s preparations. “This multilingual approach is intended to overcome language barriers and ensure that the message reaches all segments of society, particularly rural communities,” he said. Aboki said INEC had scheduled the nationwide mock exercise for Saturday, November 28, 2026, to test the operational readiness of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Election Results Viewing Portal (IReV), while familiarising voters with the technology ahead of the 2027 polls. He urged registered voters in the state to verify whether their polling units were among those selected for the exercise by visiting INEC’s official website, www.inecnigeria.org. The commissioner also called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth groups and civil society organisations to mobilise eligible voters in the selected centres. He urged media organisations to amplify verified electoral information and avoid spreading misinformation, while warning against attempts to disrupt the exercise. “Government wishes to state unequivocally that any individual or group of persons who engages in acts capable of causing political instability, disrupting the electoral process, or inciting violence during this exercise will be dealt with in accordance with the law,” he warned. Aboki added that the state government remained committed to peaceful, issue-based political activities and would continue to partner with INEC and the media to support the conduct of credible and transparent elections in 2027. item.title: Putin unveils new nuclear submarine
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday unveiled a new nuclear-powered submarine and said Russia would add five more to the country’s fleet by 2030, according to footage released by the Kremlin. At the Sevmash shipyard in the northwestern city of Severodvinsk, Putin attended a flag-raising ceremony aboard the Perm submarine, marking its formal transfer to the navy. “Russia is one of the few countries in the world capable of building powerful nuclear submarines of this kind, weapons with global reach and significance,” he said. Nuclear-powered submarines are a key part of Russia’s nuclear deterrent because their ability to operate covertly underwater ensures a retaliatory strike capability in the event of an attack. Putin said the navy would receive five more by 2030, including three vessels from the Yasen-M class, the same class as the Perm. item.title: Keyamo pushes for 99% ICAO safety rating, tasks NAMA, NCAA
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has urged the Nigerian Airspace Management Agency, NAMA, to sustain the country’s improved safety performance through continuous monitoring, institutional collaboration and the systematic resolution of outstanding regulatory requirements. Keyamo commended NAMA for what he described as its exceptional contribution to Nigeria’s impressive performance during the recent International Civil Aviation Organisation ICAO, Coordinated Validation Mission, ICVM. The commendation followed Nigeria’s successful ICVM, conducted between April 15 and 22, 2026, during which the country recorded an Effective Implementation, EI, score of 91.30 per cent. Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Dr Abdullahi Musa, disclosed this in a letter of commendation addressed to NAMA’s Managing Director, Engr Umar Farouk. The minister specifically acknowledged the timely closure of the Significant Safety Concern, SSC, raised by the ICAO team following the validation exercise. He stated: “Keyamo recalled that upon assuming office, one of his cardinal priorities was to ensure strict adherence to aviation safety regulations and sustain a consistent upward trajectory in Nigeria’s ICAO safety rating. “According to him, the 91.30 per cent Effective Implementation score represented a significant validation of the administration’s commitment to aviation safety and had further strengthened Nigeria’s reputation among ICAO Contracting States. “While acknowledging NAMA’s contribution, Keyamo maintained that Nigeria’s improved safety performance must be sustained through continuous monitoring, institutional collaboration and the systematic resolution of outstanding regulatory requirements, even as he urged the agency to collaborate with the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to address all outstanding Protocol Questions under the Air Navigation Services, ANS, audit area, with a view to raising Nigeria’s Effective Implementation score to at least 99 per cent.” The post Keyamo pushes for 99% ICAO safety rating, tasks NAMA, NCAA appeared first on Vanguard News .

Similarly, the naira strengthened in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), appreciating to N1,376 per dollar from N1,378 per dollar recorded on Thursday. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market improved by N2 to N1,376 per dollar from N1,378. item.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau postpones elections to 2028 over inadequate technical, material condition
item.description: Guinea-Bissau’s military rulers have postponed presidential and parliamentary elections scheduled for next week by nearly two years, further delaying the country’s return to civilian rule. Transitional President, Gen. Horta N’Tam, announced in a decree that the elections, initially scheduled for December 6, would now hold on November 26, 2028. The announcement came exactly one year after the military seized power, promising to restore civilian rule within 12 months. In a statement, the presidency said an assessment of preparations for the elections had revealed insufficient “technical, material and financial conditions” to conduct the polls as scheduled. It said the postponement would provide more time to ensure that the elections were credible, transparent and inclusive, with all candidates given equal opportunities. The presidency also reaffirmed its commitment to conducting the country’s first local government elections but did not announce a date for the exercise. Gen. N’Tam was sworn in as transitional president a day after the military overthrew President Umaro Sissoco Embaló in November 2025. The coup occurred three days after general elections and a day before provisional results were expected to be announced. Both Embaló and his main challenger, Fernando Dias, had claimed victory in the election. Embaló, who has since been living in exile in Morocco, was barred from returning to Guinea-Bissau last month, despite expressing interest in contesting the elections. Guinea-Bissau has experienced several coups and attempted coups since gaining independence from Portugal in 1974. item.title: ECOWAS Speaker warns of levy shortfalls ahead of 2027 budget
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Speaker of the ECOWAS Parliament, Memounatou Ibrahima, has warned that rising public debt and mounting pressure on national finances could undermine member states’ ability to remit the Community Levy, urging governments to strengthen compliance ahead of the consideration of the regional body’s 2027 budget. Ibrahima gave the warning on Friday in Abuja during the opening of the 2026 Second Ordinary Session of the ECOWAS Parliament. She said the proposed 2027 budget was being considered at a time when member states were grappling with increasing demands for development financing and growing pressure on public finances. The Speaker urged national parliaments to intensify engagement with their respective governments to ensure regular collection and remittance of proceeds from the Community Levy. She also called on lawmakers to scrutinise budget proposals and ensure that public allocations addressed clearly identified needs and delivered measurable benefits to citizens across the region. She said: “One of the major highlights of our deliberations will be the consideration of the draft Community Budget for the 2027 financial year. “Indeed, persistent economic and financial constraints, characterised by mounting pressure on public finances and the indebtedness of our Member States, with the attendant risks to the remittance of the Community Levy, as well as increasing demands for development financing, require us to exercise particular vigilance and responsibility.” Ibrahima added: “I wish to urge our national parliaments to intensify their advocacy efforts with Member States at the appropriate political level to ensure the collection and systematic remittance of proceeds from the Community Levy.” She stressed that every budget allocation must be justified by its relevance and expected impact, while priority areas should be determined by efficiency, performance and tangible results for the people. The Speaker said the Parliament would also receive country reports and consider findings from oversight missions covering goods in transit, the ECOWAS Mission in The Gambia, regional agricultural projects and the development of a climate-friendly electricity market. She pledged to work with the new President of the ECOWAS Commission, Gen. Birame Diop, and other community institutions to advance regional integration. Ibrahima also referenced the Lungi Declaration, through which regional leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the legislative and oversight functions of the ECOWAS Parliament. She congratulated Cabo Verde’s President, José Maria Neves, on his re-election and called for peaceful elections in The Gambia and Nigeria, whose presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027. In his remarks, Diop warned that terrorism spreading from the Sahel continued to pose a threat to countries in the coastal region. item.title: Man Utd trigger Fernandes’ one-year contract extension
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United have activated a one-year option in captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract, keeping him at the club until 2028. According to the BBC, the option prevents overseas clubs from approaching the Portugal international over a pre-contract agreement when the transfer window opens on January 1. Fernandes’ previous contract was due to expire next summer. Fernandes, 32, and United are understood to have agreed to resume talks over a longer-term deal later, with their immediate focus on improving the club’s league position. The midfielder confirmed on Tuesday that contract discussions had been paused. United have been negotiating with Fernandes since the summer. He has turned down two offers, including the club’s initial proposal, but said the priority should be returning to winning ways. “I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games,” he said. Fernandes joined United from Sporting in January 2020 for £47m. He has since made 343 appearances, scoring 115 goals. Last season, he broke the Premier League assists record and won the individual player of the year awards as United finished third. United were open to selling him in the summer of 2025, when Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal made a substantial offer. After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes chose to stay, though he later said it “hurt” that the club had been willing to sell him. The captain has said he remains ambitious to win major honours at United. “My aim will always be to win the Premier League and the Champions League within the club I am,” he said. Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday’s Premier League match against Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus. He scored both goals in United’s 2-2 draw with his former club but missed training on Friday. “We are going to assess during the day and then tomorrow see how he is when he wakes up,” head coach Mauricio Pochettino said. “We are not going to take any risks.” The post Man Utd trigger Fernandes’ one-year contract extension appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Wike’s Imo campaign demand an insult, says RHGN leader
item.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Deputy National Leader (South-East) of Renewed Hope for Greater Nigeria (RHGN), Mazi Franklin Ngoforo, has described as an insult to the people of Imo State and the South-East a reported request by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, to lead President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign in the state. Ngoforo, an indigene of Imo State, said Wike’s reported demand suggested that the state lacked the political capacity and leadership structures to determine its own political direction. He questioned why a political figure from outside Imo would seek to take charge of the president’s re-election campaign in a state with a history of producing prominent national figures and successful entrepreneurs. Ngoforo, in a statement, alleged that Wike’s political ambition reflected a desire to dominate and control political affairs in the South-East rather than build genuine partnerships with the people. He warned against what he described as attempts by outsiders to assume the role of colonial masters over the region’s political space. The RHGN leader maintained that Imo State possessed the political maturity, leadership capacity and grassroots structures to determine its electoral choices without external control. He insisted that no individual could claim ownership of the state’s political destiny. Ngoforo, however, expressed confidence that President Tinubu would secure re-election in Imo State in 2027, citing the mobilisation capacity of RHGN across the state. He said members of the organisation were already engaging communities and voters, taking the Renewed Hope message to the grassroots and building support for the President. The post Wike’s Imo campaign demand an insult, says RHGN leader appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that more than $600 million of the stolen crypto has passed through THORChain, though Elliptic said that figure could count funds that went through more than once. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps. Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. Elliptic has said the launderers will still need other services, such as over-the-counter brokers, to turn the coins into cash. The FBI on Oct. 31 published

item.title: Osun LG Crisis Will Be Fully Resolved In The Next One Week — Gov Adeleke
item.description: Governor Ademola Adeleke has assured the people of Osun State that the protracted local government crisis in the state will be resolved within the next week, following President Bola Tinubu’s intervention. Governor Adeleke gave this assurance in his inaugural speech during his second-term inauguration held at Osogbo City Stadium, where he listed some of the priorities of his second-term administration across all sectors. “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter and in the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres,” he said. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke was sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. As part of his priorities, the re-elected governor promised to set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission, as well as infrastructural expansion and recruitment of teachers and rehabilitation of schools, including reviving technical colleges. He also said that job and wealth creation will be at the heart of his second term. “We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy,” Adeleke said. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” In the health sector, he said about 70 per cent of existing primary health care centres were rehabilitated and equipped with solar and power facilities in his first term. “We upgraded and completed 232 out of 332 primary health care centres. The plan was to complete the whole 332 PHCs, but the seizure of local government allocations halted the process,” the governor said. “My government made sure that our primary school teachers, healthcare professionals at our primary healthcare centres, and local government retirees got paid in the last two years.” Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. Adeleke said his vision is to move Osun from a civil service economy to an industrialised one, noting that his administration is open to partnership with private organisations and economic advisory groups. “Specifically, we will target agro-processing factories, industrial parks across districts, free trade zones, sports and tourism development, and a better business environment. “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content,” he added. President Tinubu was represented at the inauguration by the Vice President, Kashim Shettima. Other dignitaries that graced the occasion included Bisi Akande and Iyiola Omisore, other All Progressives

item.title: Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. item.title: The best Black Friday deals Ars could find
item.description: Every year has a Prime Day—some years even have two Prime Days!—where we celebrate the life and achievements of the greatest leader the Autobots have ever known: the inimitable Optimus Prime. But just as every dawn is twinned by a dusk that steals its light, so too did Optimus Prime's bright spark fade, extinguished by the foul hand of Megatron during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005 . It is a day that lives in infamy forever, and we all know the tale—how the evil Megatron (cursed be the flow of his energon!) commandeered an Autobot shuttle, cruelly murdered its crew, and launched a cowardly surprise attack against Autobot City—a plan utterly bereft of honor, as was so typical of Megatron's schemes. Even as individual Autobots strove to secure Autobot City— heroes, all of them !—hope began to fade under an onslaught that included an attack by the fearsome Devastator , against which there appeared to be no defense. And then, at the precipice of disaster, Optimus Prime made the fateful declaration whose words still ring out to this day: " Megatron must be stopped, no matter the cost ." The fearless Autobot transformed, rolled out, and got the job done—even though that cost was high. Many brave Autobots besides Optimus Prime lost their lives during the fighting. It was truly a dark day, a black day—and so, every year on the Friday after Thanksgiving, we pause to remember the noble sacrifices made by Prime and by so many others. This is why today is known as Black Friday. Read full article Comments

item.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
item.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. How and when I'm watching it The names and distances of the stars in Cassiopeia. (Image credit: Starry Night) I'm going to observe Cassiopeia twice on the same evening this week, which is about as complicated as the experiment needs to get. The first time will be shortly after darkness falls. I'll find the W, note which way it seems to be pointing and use something fixed — a rooftop, tree or chimney — to give myself a rough reference for its position. I'll return to my backyard before bed, and see where the pattern ha

item.description: Bada Akintunde-Johnson: MD/CEO Livdot Technologies Liimited. Fans who can’t make it to Lagos this December no longer have to miss it. LivDot , a new live-event streaming platform, will stream concerts by BNXN , Fola , Oxlade and Ruger live and exclusively to audiences worldwide from 19 to 22 December. The launch also rewrites the maths of a sell-out. When a 5,000-capacity concert sells out, the ticketing opportunity usually ends there. On LivDot, the same show can sell 50,000 or more streaming tickets to fans across Nigeria, Africa and the diaspora. LivDot was founded by Bada Akintunde-Johnson , former Country Manager of Paramount Skydance Africa, whose career spans MTV Base, BET, Nickelodeon and Comedy Central in Nigeria. “Imagine being in London, Houston or Toronto and experiencing the energy of Detty December in real time,” said Akintunde-Johnson. “For fans who can’t make the trip, we are curing your fear of missing out by bringing Lagos’s live entertainment to you, wherever you are.” The December lineup Exclusive streams on LivDot this season include: 12 December — The Worship Project by The Fountain of Life Church 19 December — BNXN (formerly known as Buju) 20 December — Fola 21 December — Oxlade 22 December — Ruger 25 December — Saheed Osupa and Friends White Party Date [TBC] — The Digital Product Growth Summit More headline concerts, faith and business events are lined up for the season. Fans can buy streaming tickets or watch free events at www.livdot.co Beyond the venue walls For event organizers, LivDot is the infrastructure behind that extra audience. It brings production, live streaming and payments together in one place, with content distributed free or behind a pay-per-view access fee. A built-in marketplace of vetted photographers and videographers makes hiring quality production talent easier and more consistent. “For too long, the reach and economics of live events have been defined by the walls of the venue,” said Akintunde-Johnson. “A sold-out room should be the floor of an event’s audience and earning potential, not the ceiling.” For artists, it means reaching fans abroad far more often. Instead of waiting for an occasional arena date in London or New York, an artist can stage a lean live performance in Nigeria, sell affordable digital tickets to fans worldwide, and let LivDot handle production, streaming and payment. That opens the door to intimate shows, exclusive sessions, album listenings and other fan experiences. “Artists should be able to perform more often, on their own terms, and earn directly from fans around the world,” Akintunde-Johnson added. “We want to make that commercially practical.” Concerts are only the start. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 27, 1885: Astronomer captures 1st known photo of a meteor during an Andromedid meteor storm
item.description: null On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). Meteor Shower Quiz: How Well Do You Know 'Shooting Stars'? This modern photo of the Geminid meteor shower shows dozens of meteors captured in a long exposure by Josh Drury. Ladislaus Weinek, who captured the first photo of a meteor, had to use a photographic plate in 1889. (Image credit: Josh Dury) Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors. In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. The court entered a default judgment in August 2025 that found they violated New York’s Martin Act and banned them from the securities, c

item.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
item.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. item.title: Artemis III astronauts meet their spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 27, 2026
item.description: null NASA's Artemis III astronauts pose holding up three fingers to symbolize their mission as they visit the Orion spacecraft they will ride to space. (Image credit: NASA/Kim Shiflett) Training for a mission to space is hard work. But sometimes you have to take a minute and have a little fun with your crewmates. What is it? Crowded together with the Orion spacecraft, the four astronauts that make up the Artemis III crew hold up three fingers, taking a brief pause in their rigorous training for some lighthearted crew bonding. In the snapshot , the crew — from left to right, NASA astronauts Randy Bresnick (mission commander) and Frank Rubio (mission specialist), European Space Agency astronaut Luca Parmitano (mission pilot) and NASA astronaut Andre Douglas (mission specialist) — is spotted posing alongside the same Orion spacecraft that they will fly to space as part of their mission. This brief moment of levity took place where the spacecraft currently resides at the Neil A. Armstrong Operations and Checkout Building at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Why is it incredible? This crew has a serious mission ahead of them. The four astronauts will launch to low-Earth orbit around Earth where they plan to practice rendezvous and docking with both Blue Origin and SpaceX's lunar landing vehicles , Blue Moon and Starship, respectively. To prepare, the crew has to undergo months of critical training to both be physically ready while prepared to handle any situation that might come up during their mission. And while Artemis III isn't landing astronauts on the moon, it is a critical step toward that goal. If Artemis III goes to plan and NASA has a lunar landing vehicle that passes rendezvous and docking tests with the Orion spacecraft, Artemis IV might see astronauts land on the moon for the first time since the final Apollo mission in 1972.

item.description: Affordable laptops are even more affordable right now. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge Laptop prices have been a hot-button topic all year long thanks to RAMageddon . We’ve seen existing models get more expensive and new models arrive at higher prices than last-gen — sometimes with lower specs, too. 2026 in general has been a bad time to buy a computer. But thankfully, Black Friday can offer a tiny bit of respite. If the computer you currently use is working well for you, good. Happy for you. But if you’re in the market for something more powerful, bigger, smaller, thinner, etc. — and you prefer new over used — you can currently save some decent dough on MacBooks, Windows notebooks, and gaming laptops. The big, multi-hundred-dollar savings are typically reserved for higher-end models with bigger specs, like Windows models running Nvidia’s new Arm-based RTX Spark platform — which are getting their first major discounts. More budget-friendly laptops are also receiving decent discounts right now, though, including the MacBook Neo. The current $100 discount on Apple’s budget laptop might seem like small potatoes considering it’s just a return to its original price , but it’s the best you can do for now (if you can’t hold out for a rumored new one in 2027 ). As always, the deals below are for laptops we’ve reviewed or tested firsthand in some way at The Verge — either that exact model or a similar one we expect to be equally good. There are many laptops out there and myriad deals running now through Cyber Monday, but if any of these fit your needs, you can’t go wrong. MacBook Neo Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review . item.title: NASA’s NG-25 Mission to Launch Pioneering Space Crops Research
item.description: Experiments in the Ohalo III facility (pictured above) aim to validate plant-water delivery, optimize volume, and advance crop-production research. These insights could inform the design of plant production systems for future deep-space missions. NASA NASA experiments, including a first-of-its-kind space crop production system, will travel to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency. Investigations from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division will advance research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration, expanding knowledge of space crops and human health. Groundbreaking space crops Astronauts will need sustainable sources of food to travel farther and stay longer in space. To help understand how crop production works in microgravity, NASA is launching a novel space crops experiment . The new prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing safe, nutritious, and reliable crop production systems for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Knowledge gained from the space crop production system also could help inform agricultural practices such as vertical farming and indoor growing systems. Researchers will use this investigation to validate the system’s water delivery and volume optimization technology aboard the space station. Tiny brain models aboard station A precision health investigation is the next step toward enabling long-duration studies of human brain tissues in space. The research builds on a previous investigation that sent small, lab-grown models of the human brain, called miBrains, to the space station. This experiment will validate a miniature fluid-handling system designed to mix, deliver, and maintain the nutrient-rich liquid needed to keep the tissues alive. Researchers could use the findings to help identify potential neurological risks associated with spaceflight and develop strategies to protect astronaut health. It also may advance human tissue research and neurological disease modeling on Earth. Biological & Physical Sciences Division NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division pioneers scientific discovery and enables exploration by using space environments to conduct investigations not possible on Earth. Studying biological and physical phenomena under extreme conditions allows researchers to advance the fundamental scientific knowledge required to go farther and stay longer in space, while also benefitting life on Earth.

item.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
item.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. Tech futures lead the risk rebound Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%. “There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. The S&P 500 is headed for its best week since April, though it remains on course for its worst November since 2008. Bitcoin price has followed that rebound but lagged it. The major U.S. stock indexes are each up around 4% on the week, and silver jumped about 7% to above $44 an ounce on Friday while gold added 2.5% to above $3,670. Stocks close early at 1 p.m. ET, and the bond market shuts at 2 p.m. Rate hike bets and ETF outflows linger The macro backdrop still weighs on the bitcoin price. Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike in December after data this week showed the economy grew faster than first estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October, Reuters reported. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.84%. Spot bitcoin ETFs are also still losing cash. The U.S. funds lost $453 million on Wednesday, their seventh straight day of outflows, with BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounting for $329.7 million. That pushed November outflows to about $5.39 billion, extending what was already a record month for the funds. item.title: Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, saying the technical signal behind it failed after seven straight weeks of losses and that the bear market is “very likely not over.” Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, laid out the reversal in a report published Wednesday and sent to clients a day earlier. “We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June,” the report said. “The signal it rested on has failed.” The firm’s Oct. 26 note had argued that bitcoin had entered an accumulation phase. Galaxy said at the time that a weekly close back below the 50-week moving average that was not regained within a month would invalidate its technical case. That is what happened. Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 8 at $74,968, 0.7% below the 50-week average, after seven weekly closes above it. It then closed the week ended Nov. 15 below the 200-week average, which Galaxy has described as the floor of past bear markets. Galaxy points to $58,525 The week ended Nov. 22 closed at $61,104, 17.9% below the 50-week average and 10.4% below the 200-week average of $68,159. Bitcoin traded below its July 1 intraday low on Nov. 20 and reached $55,100 on Nov. 21, but the June 30 closing low of $58,525 held on a daily basis through Nov. 22. Galaxy now treats that level as the line to watch. A daily close below $58,525 would be “the start of a move to a materially lower low,” the report said, and the firm would not treat such a close as a buying signal by itself. History is not kind to breaks like that. In the seven prior bear market cases where bitcoin closed below a low that had stood for at least 60 days, the eventual low was at least 17% lower, with a median of 52%. Applied to the June low, that works out to about $48,500 and $28,200. Bitcoin briefly slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday morning as the Nasdaq sank, but it ended the day back above $60,000 and has not posted a daily close below $58,525. It traded near $60,800 on Thursday morning. Late by the clock, early by the depth Galaxy said two readings of the market disagree. By the calendar, this bear is old: Nov. 22 was day 412 since the Oct. 6, 2025, record, longer than the 163 to 406 days from high to low in the four prior bear markets. By depth, it looks unfinished. Bitcoin’s 53% decline compares with drops of 77% to 93% in earlier bears. It also has not closed a day below its realized price of $53,205, something every prior bear did for at least 140 days, and only two of the 13 bottom signals Galaxy tracks have been met. “The clock says this bear is overdue to end, the depth says it has further to fall, and we do not believe the price record alone can settle which,” the report said. Flows have not helped. Galaxy estimates U.S. spot bitcoin ETPs hold about 1.24 million BTC, 9.7% below their October 2025 peak, after shedding 71,339 BTC, or $4.95 billion, since Oct. 4.
